reasoning: Someone asks how the margin for selling options is worked out. A how-it-works question with no capital problem stated, so no pain.

An option seller asks how to place hedged orders to get the margin benefit after the June margin change, and whether the full margin is needed upfront. How a margin rule change affects them fits this pain, though this change seems to give hedged trades a benefit.
A trader asks how to reduce the margin needed to sell options. Looking for a way around too little capital is this pain, as in the batch before.
A Bank Nifty option seller asks how much margin an unhedged call and put need. A how-much question with no capital problem stated, so no pain.

A trader asks how to size an options position, giving the stock levels and the option's price. A how-to question with no problem stated.

Someone asks what happens if an option seller's loss grows beyond the margin paid. Ending up owing the broker is part of this pain, but it is a general question with no loss reported, as in earlier batches.

Someone asks why the government plans a high tax on F&O in the coming budget by treating derivatives like a lottery. A policy change that hits F&O traders is closest to this pain, though it is a tax plan rather than a SEBI rule and the asker may be a critic.

Someone asks how to save tax on F&O income. How F&O income is taxed and filed is this pain, though this asks about lowering tax rather than a filing problem.
Someone missed the deadline to answer an IRS CP2000 notice (a letter about income missing from a return). Nothing shows the income came from trading.
Someone got an IRS CP2000 notice with a bill after doing their own taxes. The cut-off text does not show the income came from trading.
A trader asks whether trading options can get them marked as a pattern day trader. That rule is this pain, as in earlier batches.
Someone asks how exercised options are matched to the original writer when contracts keep changing hands. A how-it-works question with no loss or surprise stated.
An active trader asks whether a service alerts traders to option price mismatches. It names no cost or doubt about a service, so no pain is tagged.
A general question on whether the IRS changes a return when someone disputes a CP2000 notice. Nothing ties it to trading.
An encyclopedia page about a futures exchange. Reference, not a trader's problem.
Someone asks for the best advanced tools and indicators for options and the 'secrets' most people miss. A request for tips with no cost or problem stated.
Someone plans to trade options with 2,000 rupees or 30 dollars and asks the most they could win or lose. A risk question; it states no loss and no capital block, so no pain.

An encyclopedia page about a type of loan. Unrelated to trading.

A trader's MetaTrader 5 app (a forex trading app) says trading is disabled and to contact the broker. An account or app problem that no pain covers; forex, not options.
